question.text: An increase in risk-free interest rates will cause:

answer.text: Call premium to increase and Put premium to decrease
Both call and put premiums to increase
Both call and put premiums to decrease
Call premium to decrease and Put premium to increase

explanation.text: The Logic: Higher risk-free interest rates increase call premium and decrease put premium. This is consistent with call rho being positive and put rho being negative under standard option-pricing models. The Trap: Unlike volatility and time-to-expiry, which generally move call and put premiums in the same direction, interest rate changes move them in opposite directions because of the differing sign of rho for calls and puts. Note: Workbook references — p.72 and p.75 (higher interest rates increase call premium and decrease put premium; positive call rho and negative put rho).
